title: First Followers
summary: Get your first Threads followers from zero, one person at a time: find 10 newcomers and small creators in your niche, and your agent stages each comment in your voice and follows at the right step while you just press Post; it learns from your edits and tracks progress - works with no post history, with copy mode when there is no browser control.
triggers: i have zero followers on threads
how do i get followers on threads with no posts
stage comments for me on threads
welcome new people on threads for me

inputs.name: connected account, a browser or computer-use tool signed in to the same Threads account (or copy mode), voice from the Threadify Brain or three short answers

outputs.name: 10-person batch with one approval, comments staged one at a time for the owner to publish, follows at the planned step, staged-vs-published learning summary, voice rules saved to the Brain only on yes, private local ledger, counts-only scoreboard, optional three scheduled posts

free_capabilities: visible-browser Threads search for newcomers (1-2 posts) and small active creators in your niche
comments staged one at a time in the Threads reply box for the owner to publish, with follows at the planned step after one batch approval
copy mode when no browser control is available: the owner pastes, posts and follows
local draft checker for plan shapes, endings, daily caps, links, duplicates, flattery templates, DMs, line breaks and specific references
local staged-vs-published diff for the learning summary (length, emoji, casing, phrases)
private local ledger with hashed handles and counts, used for 30-day dedupe, daily caps and the follow-back re-check
local casing guard that proves lower(original) == lower(final) for every optional post
self-contained local scoreboard served on 127.0.0.1, counts only
paid_capability_stubs: optional Threadify post generation counts toward the plan's AI generations

must_show: the people in the batch with post count and plan (1 comment or 3, follow step)
action: stage comments one at a time for the owner to publish and follow at the step shown
exact voice rules before any Brain save
for optional posts: three exact posts, three local dates and times, and the schedule action

instructions: The agent may type into a reply composer and click Follow only within the batch approval; it never clicks Post, Publish or reply-send and never presses Enter in a composer; the owner publishes every comment.
Never unfollow, like, repost, quote or DM.
Without a browser or computer-use tool, use copy mode: show each comment with its post link and the owner pastes, posts and follows.
When the browser is signed in to a different Threads account than Threadify, stop before any search and ask the owner to switch.
Stop at once on any Threads warning, action block, rate limit or captcha.
When a staged comment is not found published after one re-read, mark it skipped and never retype or resend it.
When Threads search finds fewer than 10 fitting people, say so and continue with fewer; never pad the list.
Never save voice rules to the Brain without the owner's yes, or their saved 'always' preference.
Never create a recurring run before the owner says yes and picks the time.
Never write the optional posts yourself when Threadify generation is unavailable; report the exact blocker and manual next step.
When a follower or post count is not readable, show it as unknown, never 0.

must_prove: account match between Threadify and the visible browser, or copy mode
starting follower and post counts with timestamp
voice source (Brain, reply settings, owner samples or low-confidence default)
batch size, plans and draft checker result
comments staged, published, edited and skipped, and follows, as counts
staged-vs-published learning summary and any voice rules saved with Brain readback
ledger recorded (counts only in the receipt)
follower count at wrap-up and the re-check counts since start
optional posts: models, casing guard, approval reply, scheduled slots and readback
schedule offer outcome and readback when created
